definitions.explanation: Chestnuts that have been roasted, typically in their shells. A popular autumn and winter street food in Japan and many other countries.

examples.english: When autumn comes, roasted chestnut stalls appear.

examples.japanese: ほくほく⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{焼|や}き{栗|ぐり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{散歩|さんぽ}する→散歩する：26840_sanposuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。
examples.english: I like walking while eating hot, fluffy roasted chestnuts.

examples.japanese: {天津|てんしん}⟦{甘栗|あまぐり}→甘栗：28493_amaguri⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧{焼|や}き{栗|ぐり}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{見|み}かける→見かける：01644_mikakeru⟧。
examples.english: Roasted chestnuts called Tianjin sweet chestnuts are commonly seen in Japan too.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ (roasting) and ⟦{栗|くり}→栗：04387_kuri⟧ (chestnut), with rendaku changing くり to ぐり. Roasted chestnuts are a quintessential autumn treat in Japan, strongly associated with the season alongside ⟦{焼|や}き{芋|いも}→焼き芋：15650_yakiimo⟧ (roasted sweet potato).

Street vendors selling {天津|てんしん}⟦{甘栗|あまぐり}→甘栗：28493_amaguri⟧ (Tianjin sweet chestnuts) are a common sight in Japanese cities during the colder months. The chestnuts are typically roasted in a rotating drum with small pebbles, which distributes heat evenly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼|や}き{栗|ぐり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{屋台|やたい}→屋台：10549_yatai⟧: roasted chestnut stall
- {天津|てんしん}⟦{甘栗|あまぐり}→甘栗：28493_amaguri⟧: Tianjin sweet chestnuts (a well-known brand/style)
- ほくほく⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{焼|や}き{栗|ぐり}: hot, fluffy roasted chestnuts

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{栗|くり}→栗：04387_kuri⟧: chestnut — the base ingredient
- ⟦{甘栗|あまぐり}→甘栗：28493_amaguri⟧: sweet roasted chestnuts — specifically the sugar-glazed or naturally sweet variety
- ⟦{焼|や}き{芋|いも}→焼き芋：15650_yakiimo⟧: roasted sweet potato — another beloved autumn street food
